stem: In Ibn Ishaq's sirah, what word does Bilal ibn Rabah repeat in Mecca while his master Umayyah has a great rock laid on his chest?
options: haqq, haqq: 'Truth, Truth'
ahad, ahad: 'One, One'
salam, salam: 'Peace, Peace'
nur, nur: 'Light, Light'
why: Under the rock in the midday heat, Bilal answers only "Ahad, ahad", One, One, refusing the idols; Abu Bakr later buys and frees him. Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah; compare Qur'an 112:1.
source: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (Ibn Hisham's recension)

es.stem: En la sira de Ibn Ishaq, ¿qué palabra repite Bilal ibn Rabah en La Meca mientras su amo Umayyah le pone una gran roca sobre el pecho?
options: haqq, haqq: 'Verdad, Verdad'
ahad, ahad: 'Uno, Uno'
salam, salam: 'Paz, Paz'
nur, nur: 'Luz, Luz'
es.why: Bajo la roca, en el calor del mediodía, Bilal solo responde "Ahad, ahad", Uno, Uno, rechazando a los ídolos; después Abu Bakr lo compra y lo libera. Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah; compara con Corán 112:1.

stem: Which companion earned the name dhat al-nitaqayn, 'she of the two belts', on the night of the hijrah to Medina?
options: Umm Ayman, the Prophet's nurse
Fatimah, the Prophet's daughter
Asma, the daughter of Abu Bakr
Aisha, the daughter of Abu Bakr
why: Finding nothing to tie the food bag and water skin for the Prophet ﷺ and her father, Asma bint Abi Bakr tore her waistband in two and was called she of the two belts. Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Merits of the Ansar.
source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab Manaqib al-Ansar (hadith of the hijrah)

es.stem: ¿Qué compañera recibió el nombre de dhat al-nitaqayn, 'la de los dos cinturones', la noche de la hégira a Medina?
options: Umm Ayman, la nodriza del Profeta
Fátima, la hija del Profeta
Asma, la hija de Abu Bakr
Aisha, la hija de Abu Bakr
es.why: Como no había con qué atar la bolsa de comida y el odre de agua del Profeta ﷺ y de su padre, Asma bint Abi Bakr partió su cinturón en dos y la llamaron la de los dos cinturones. Sahih al-Bujari, Libro de los méritos de los Ansar.

stem: In Sahih al-Bukhari, after the first revelation at Hira, on what grounds does Khadijah tell the Prophet ﷺ that Allah will never disgrace him?
options: his descent from Ibrahim through Banu Hashim
his long seclusion and prayer on Mount Hira
a dream of light she had seen before their marriage
his care for kin, the weak, the poor and guests
why: Khadijah answers from how he treats people: he keeps ties of kinship, carries the burden of the weak, gives to the destitute, honors guests and helps in true hardship. Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Revelation, hadith 3 (from Aisha).
source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab Bad' al-Wahy, hadith 3

es.stem: En Sahih al-Bujari, después de la primera revelación en Hira, ¿en qué se basa Jadiya para decirle al Profeta ﷺ que Allah nunca lo deshonrará?
options: su linaje desde Ibrahim por el clan de Banu Hashim
su largo retiro y oración en el monte Hira
un sueño de luz que tuvo antes de casarse con él
su cuidado de parientes, débiles, pobres y huéspedes
es.why: Jadiya responde a partir de cómo él trata a la gente: mantiene los lazos de parentesco, carga con el peso del débil, da al que no tiene, honra al huésped y ayuda en la verdadera desgracia. Sahih al-Bujari, Libro del comienzo de la revelación, hadiz 3 (de Aisha).

stem: In the hadith of the Mi'raj in Sahih al-Bukhari, why are the fifty daily prayers first given reduced to five?
options: Musa urges him to go back and ask for less
Jibril pleads that his people are too weak
Ibrahim counsels him to seek a lighter load
Isa warns the burden will be too heavy
why: Coming down with fifty prayers, the Prophet ﷺ passes Musa, who says his community cannot bear it and sends him back to ask for less, again and again, until five remain with the reward of fifty. Sahih al-Bukhari (Malik ibn Sa'sa'a; Abu Dharr).
source: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith of the Mi'raj (Malik ibn Sa'sa'a; Abu Dharr)

es.stem: En el hadiz del Miraj en Sahih al-Bujari, ¿por qué las cincuenta oraciones diarias que se dieron al principio se reducen a cinco?
options: Musa le insiste en volver y pedir menos
Yibril ruega porque su pueblo es muy débil
Ibrahim le aconseja buscar una carga más ligera
Isa le advierte que la carga será muy pesada
es.why: Al bajar con cincuenta oraciones, el Profeta ﷺ pasa junto a Musa, quien le dice que su comunidad no podrá soportarlo y lo manda a pedir menos, una y otra vez, hasta que quedan cinco con la recompensa de cincuenta. Sahih al-Bujari (Malik ibn Sa'sa'a; Abu Dharr).

stem: At the Battle of Uhud, why does the fighting turn against the Muslims after their strong start?
options: a sandstorm blinds the Muslim ranks at noon
the Meccans seize the wells behind their lines
the archers leave their hill to gather spoils
fresh troops from Ta'if reach the Meccan side
why: The archers had been told not to leave their hill; seeing the Meccans flee, most go down for the spoils despite Abdullah ibn Jubayr's reminder, and the battle turns. Sahih al-Bukhari (al-Bara' ibn Azib); Qur'an 3:152.
source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Maghazi (al-Bara' ibn Azib); Qur'an 3:152

es.stem: En la batalla de Uhud, ¿por qué el combate se vuelve contra los musulmanes después de su buen comienzo?
options: una tormenta de arena ciega a las filas musulmanas
los mecanos toman los pozos detrás de sus líneas
los arqueros dejan su colina para tomar el botín
llegan tropas frescas de Taif al lado mecano
es.why: A los arqueros se les había ordenado no dejar su colina; al ver huir a los mecanos, la mayoría baja por el botín pese al recordatorio de Abdullah ibn Yubayr, y la batalla cambia. Sahih al-Bujari (al-Bara' ibn Azib); Corán 3:152.

stem: Under the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah as Sahih al-Bukhari records its terms, a young man of Mecca becomes Muslim and flees to Medina without his guardian's leave. What does the treaty require?
options: Medina may keep him, since he is now a Muslim
Medina may keep him if it pays Quraysh a ransom
Medina must let him choose the city he lives in
Medina must send him back to Quraysh in Mecca
why: Suhayl's terms say any man who comes from Quraysh to the Muslims, even one who follows their religion, must be returned; so Abu Jandal and then Abu Basir were handed back, though Quraysh owed no such return. Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Conditions (al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwan).
source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Shurut, hadith 2731-2732 (al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwan)

es.stem: Según el Tratado de Hudaybiyya tal como Sahih al-Bujari registra sus términos, un joven de La Meca se hace musulmán y huye a Medina sin permiso de su tutor. ¿Qué exige el tratado?
options: Medina puede quedárselo, porque ya es musulmán
Medina puede quedárselo si paga un rescate a Quraysh
Medina debe dejarle elegir la ciudad donde vivir
Medina debe devolverlo a Quraysh en La Meca
es.why: Los términos de Suhayl dicen que todo hombre que llegue de Quraysh a los musulmanes, aunque siga su religión, debe ser devuelto; por eso Abu Yandal y después Abu Basir fueron entregados, aunque Quraysh no debía una devolución así. Sahih al-Bujari, Libro de las condiciones (al-Miswar ibn Majrama y Marwan).

stem: What was the Hilf al-Fudul, the 'league of the virtuous' formed in Mecca before the revelation, and how did the Prophet ﷺ later speak of it?
why: Clans of Quraysh met at the house of Abdullah ibn Jud'an and swore to stand with anyone wronged in Mecca, native or stranger, until his right was restored; the young Prophet ﷺ was present, and later said he would not trade having witnessed it for red camels, and would answer such a call even in Islam. Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah.
source: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (Ibn Hisham's recension)

rubric.point: Says it was a pact among Meccan clans to stand together with anyone wronged, local or stranger, until what was taken was given back. 'A peace treaty between tribes' or 'an alliance for war' does not count.

Says the Prophet ﷺ later praised it: he would not trade having been there for red camels (or any great prize), or he would answer such a call even after Islam came. Saying only that 'he took part in it' counts as partly.
Mentions that it met at the house of Abdullah ibn Jud'an, or that it was made before prophethood among people who still served idols (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: ¿Qué fue el Hilf al-Fudul, la 'liga de los virtuosos' formada en La Meca antes de la revelación, y cómo habló después el Profeta ﷺ de ella?
es.why: Clanes de Quraysh se reunieron en la casa de Abdullah ibn Yud'an y juraron ponerse del lado de cualquiera que sufriera una injusticia en La Meca, fuera de la ciudad o extranjero, hasta que se le devolviera su derecho; el joven Profeta ﷺ estuvo presente, y más tarde dijo que no cambiaría haberlo presenciado por camellos rojos, y que respondería a ese llamado incluso en el islam. Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah.

stem: When Quraysh sent envoys to the Negus (al-Najashi) of Abyssinia to bring back the Muslim emigrants, what did Ja'far ibn Abi Talib recite to him, and how did the king respond?
why: Asked to recite something of the revelation, Ja'far read the opening of Surah Maryam; the Negus wept until his beard was wet, said this and what was brought before came from one source, and refused to hand the Muslims over, returning Quraysh's gifts. Musnad Ahmad (Umm Salamah); Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah.
source: Musnad Ahmad (report of Umm Salamah); Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah

rubric.point: Names Surah Maryam (the chapter about Mary, with Zakariyya, Yahya and the birth of Isa) as what Ja'far recited. 'Some verses of the Qur'an' with no further detail counts as partly.
Says the king was moved (wept) and refused to hand the Muslims over to the Quraysh envoys, letting them stay under his protection. Saying only that 'he liked it' does not count.
Mentions that the Negus said this message and what Musa or Isa brought came from one source, or that he returned Quraysh's gifts (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: Cuando Quraysh envió emisarios al Negus (al-Nayashi) de Abisinia para que le devolviera a los emigrantes musulmanes, ¿qué le recitó Ya'far ibn Abi Talib y cómo respondió el rey?
es.why: Cuando le pidieron recitar algo de la revelación, Ya'far leyó el comienzo de la sura Maryam; el Negus lloró hasta mojarse la barba, dijo que esto y lo que se había traído antes venían de una misma fuente, y se negó a entregar a los musulmanes, devolviendo los regalos de Quraysh. Musnad Ahmad (Umm Salamah); Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah.
